profile.headline: Software Software Engineer
profile.summary: Software engineer specializing in performance engineering, with a focus on understanding how hardware and software interact at a low level. My work spans Linux Systems and Kubernetes, on large-scale bare metal and cloud platforms, with hands-on depth in areas like DPDK, eBPF, RDMA, GPU-accelerated networking, and NUMA-aware memory management. I have contributed to academic research on high-performance networking models and independently implemented GPU Direct RDMA-based packet processing pipelines. I am drawn to problems that sit at the boundary of systems engineering and low-level development, and I am actively building toward systems-level engineering roles, in HPC or GPU-intensive Linux environments. Open to connecting with others working in these spaces.

projects.title: VectorFlow-GX: GPU-accelerated Inline Packet Processing
projects.description: Implemented a GPU-accelerated inline packet processing pipeline leveraging GPUDirect RDMA and CUDA kernels, a technology that enables packets to bypass the CPU on the data path entirely, transferring directly from an RDMA-capable NIC to GPU memory over PCIe via DMA, while the CPU handles only lightweight control plane orchestration via a communication list. The idea was inspired by an NVIDIA researcher's blog, Boosting Inline Packet Processing Using DPDK and GPUdev with GPUs, which introduced me to this concept. Development began with a DPDK-based prototype before pivoting to NVIDIA's DOCA GPUNetIO library, a more purpose-built abstraction for this use case, albeit with compatibility limited to the Mellanox ConnectX BlueField-2.

projects.title: HPC Research Project
projects.description: Researched and implemented network services for the Exposed Buffer Architecture, a high-throughput model for low-latency networking in HPC, in collaboration with Prof. Micah Beck at the University of Tennessee. Contributions included developing a shared C library, contributing memory-management code to an EBA implementation, and authoring an OMNeT++ network simulation in C++.
